feature: A sound's waveform follows its fades and level
summary: A sound's waveform on the timeline is now drawn at the level it plays at: a fade in rises out of a hairline, a fade out sinks into one, and dragging the level line down shrinks the waveform with it while you drag.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/a-sound-s-waveform-follows-its-level-walk.json.

try.do: Open a recording with somebody talking in it (the walk uses the talk sample the captions tutorial opens) and click its sound under V1.
Drag the diamond at the top left of the sound to the right, to about one second, and watch the waveform before you let go.
Let go: the first second of the waveform rises from a hairline to full height.
Drag the level line down a little and watch the waveform while the button is still down.
Let go: the whole waveform stays smaller, the fade still rising at its start.
Compare with the lanes in the audio mock, where the music fades in, dips under the voice and fades out.
Mute the track from its header: the waveform does not change, only level and fades do.

evaluate: Does the fade in read as a fade at a glance, without looking at the level line?
Turned down by about 9 dB the waveform draws at about a third of its height. Is that the right amount of shrink, or does it read as too quiet?
Does the waveform following the hand during the drag feel connected to the line, or would you rather it settled after you let go?
rough: Below the recorded level the drawing is scaled straight by the level, as the mock does (samp times level), so a fade visibly rises; above it, a boost grows the drawing the way gain does, so twice as loud never draws twice as tall. Matches the mock's rule.

The mock's lanes are 84 points tall and draw the waveform as one smooth filled shape; ours are 36 points and draw thin bars. This difference was there before this task and is covered by a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-s-and-its-wa.
The mock's fade diamonds are 12 point white diamonds shown at all times; ours are small and show on hover or pick. Covered by fade-handles-and-level-points-look-like-the-mock.
The mock's music dips under the voice by itself (duck); that is out of scope here and covered by the decision card music-dips-under-the-speech-by-itself-when-you-put-music-under-someone.
The fade diamond, the level line and the waveform are shared code, so the Current release draws the same thing wherever it shows a sound's bar.
